version.changelog:
1.0.1: Bump to dodge ClawHub version conflict on initial submit.

- No functional changes—version increment only.
- Ensures compatibility and avoids version collision during initial ClawHub publication.
- Previous content and orchestration logic remain unchanged.

llm.summary: This skill is a documented guide and read-only router for governance sub-skills, with no evidence of hidden data access, network use, persistence, or automatic actions.

dimensions.detail: The manifest allows Read, Grep, and Bash, which is enough to view files and run the router; Bash is broader than the script strictly needs but is disclosed and not used for unsafe behavior in the artifact.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The package contains Markdown documentation and one small Python CLI script with no dependencies, installer behavior, remote fetches, or generated hooks.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Instructions are scoped to listing governance stages and advising users which sub-skill to invoke; it does not auto-run those sub-skills or alter agent behavior.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No persistence, privilege escalation, credential handling, background workers, memory writes, file mutation, or business-data changes were found.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The stated purpose is to provide an end-to-end AI governance playbook and route users to nine independently published sub-skills by slug; the inspected script only prints static routing information.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Installers should treat this as a table of contents, not a complete security tool. It appears safe as a router, but each referenced sub-skill should be reviewed separately before use, especially those that handle prompts, documents, badges, release gates, or kill-switch workflows.
